lines: It did its job without complaint. That is the highest compliment a tool gets.
The gear held when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Those marks show it earned its place in the fight.
Let me see it. The wear will tell me where the strain landed.
That edge took a hard blow and stayed true.
The grip is worn where you held on. I can wrap it again.
There is a new chip near the tip, but it can be ground out.
You used it properly. The damage is honest.
The head stayed tight through combat. I fitted it well.
Clean the blood off before rust finds the scratches.
That dent means it met something heavier than expected.
The handle flexed without splitting. Good wood proves itself that way.
I can tell you blocked with this more than once.
It needs oil and a little time on the stone before the next fight.
The balance has shifted from that strike. Hand it over.
You brought it back used, not abused. I appreciate the difference.
This saw real danger and gave you one less thing to worry about.
The binding loosened, but nothing failed when it mattered.
I will repair the damage. Keep the story if you want it.
It is worn, dirty, and still serviceable. Good result.
Still untouched. Sometimes the best fight is the one that never reaches your gear.
Not a scratch on it. I hope that means you stayed out of reach.
The edge is as clean as when it left my bench.
You carried it but never needed it. That is not a failure.
The grip has no wear from combat. Keep it ready anyway.
Good. No blood, no chips, no repair needed.
It stayed in its loop the whole time by the look of it.
Unused gear can still do its job by giving you a choice.
Nothing tested this one. I prefer that to patching a broken handle.
The balance is unchanged. You did not swing it once.
Keep the edge oiled even when it sees no action.
You brought it home exactly as I gave it to you.
There is only dust on this. A cloth will handle that.
No impact marks at all. The danger must have passed elsewhere.
It was ready if you needed it. That matters.
Do not be embarrassed that it stayed unused. You came back safe.
The sheath did more work than the blade this time.
I will check the fittings, though I doubt anything shifted.
Better an idle tool than an injured hand.
Put it away dry and it will be ready for the next alarm.
